arguments.brief:
## Goal
Design a caching layer for a Postgres-backed API that brings p99 latency from 120 ms to under 40 ms without ever serving stale balances.

## Context
Load: about 2k requests/s; reads outnumber writes 20:1; most data is per-user. Balances must be read-your-writes consistent. Everything else may be up to a few seconds stale (assumption).

## Constraints
Answer in one reply; no tools. Keep Postgres as the source of truth.

## Acceptance
- A design with cache placement, keys, invalidation, and failure behaviour.
- An argument that balances are never stale, and a latency estimate under 40 ms.

## Output format
A one-paragraph summary, then sections: components, data flow, invalidation, failure modes, expected latency.

reference.content: Recommended design: a per-user read-through cache in Redis with write-through invalidation of balances via a transactional outbox, so balances are never stale; the estimate is p99 25-35 ms. Details follow from the design report ...
